html:
Ögedei was the third son of Genghis Khan and the second great khan of the Mongol Empire, from 1229 to 1241.

Genghis chose him as heir over his older brothers because he was calm and good at keeping peace among the family. His reign carried the empire to its greatest push in every direction:

  • He finished the conquest of the Jin dynasty of north China in 1234, ending the Liao and Jin era.
  • He sent his nephew Batu and the general Subutai west. They conquered the Volga Bulgars and the Rus principalities, took Kiev in 1240, and invaded Poland and Hungary in 1241.
  • His armies attacked Korea and Song China and completed the conquest of Iran.

He also built the state. He walled the capital Karakorum in 1235, set up the Yam relay stations across the empire, ordered a census, and on the advice of the Khitan minister Yelü Chucai taxed north China rather than emptying it.

He drank heavily and died in December 1241. His death is often given as the reason Batu's armies pulled back from central Europe.
sum: Ögedei was the third son of Genghis Khan and the second great khan of the Mongol Empire, from 1229 to 1241.
